title: A tail-recursive sum
starter:
let rec sum_from acc l =
  match l with
  | [] -> 0
  | x :: rest -> sum_from (acc + x) rest
hints: The recursive case is already tail recursive. Trace `sum_from 0 [1; 2]` by hand: what is `acc` when you reach `[]`?
When the list is empty, the whole answer is already in `acc`. The base case throws it away.
explain: With an accumulator, the running total travels down in `acc`, so when the list runs out the answer is `acc` itself. Returning 0 there loses everything that was added on the way. The recursive call is the last thing the function does, so it is a tail call and uses no extra stack.
